intro: Look out to the Maiden's Tower, a monument in İstanbul province, on an islet off Üsküdar. Its first structure goes back to the 5th century BC. Over time it has been many things: first a customs post, later a quarantine station, a lighthouse and a watchtower. The building standing today dates from the eighteenth century.
history: The first structure on this islet off Üsküdar was raised in the fifth century BC by the Athenian commander Alcibiades — to tax the ships passing the strait. Under Byzantium the islet anchored a chain drawn to the opposite shore. Under the Ottomans it served as a quarantine station, a lighthouse and a watchtower. The building standing today dates from the eighteenth century.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the lighthouse tower, the quay, the domed hall and the lamp room.
facts: Did you know? The tower was once a cholera quarantine station: the sick from ships arriving at İstanbul were put ashore right here. And its story is older than you might think — the first structure on the islet was raised in the fifth century BC by the Athenian commander Alcibiades, to tax the ships passing through.
outro: This brings our tour of the Maiden's Tower to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. A tower that has watched over ships for so long deserves a fond farewell. Enjoy your visit.
